title: Typed handoffs: assignment and deliverable as contracts
situation: Every role's profile names its assignment (for the lead, a cut brief) and its deliverable (for the lead, the outcome with its efficiency), but only as text. Nothing checked that a lead was handed a cut brief, so example 19's scenario, which never gave it one, ran three live batches before the omission was found (0062). Agent frameworks type the handoff (an input type checked when an agent is called, a structured output it must return), and omp already validates a subagent's output against a declared schema.
decision: Each assignment and deliverable value carries a schema of what it holds, in the design's terms: a cut brief holds the cut's concepts, examples and decisions in force; a deliverable holds, per example, its concept and outcome, with the verdicts and efficiency figures. The binding checks the assignment when an agent is dispatched or launched and refuses one that does not fit, naming what is missing, and binds the deliverable as the harness's own output schema. Behavioral evaluation scenarios are built from the same schema, so a scenario that omits a role's inputs fails at once.
consequences: Realized with 0059 in the cut after the execution cut. The assignment and deliverable values in the master design gain their schemas there; the check that a scenario fits its role's assignment is part of offline proof.
